# CCTV Buying Guide

This guide helps customers choose surveillance equipment based on their application and requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 1: Determine the Installation Location

Typical installation locations include

- Home
- Apartment
- Villa
- Retail Shop
- Office
- Warehouse
- Factory
- School
- Hospital
- Hotel
- Parking Area
- Farm
- Construction Site

The installation environment influences camera type, resolution, weather resistance, lens selection, and storage requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 2: Choose Camera Technology

IP Cameras

Advantages

- Higher image quality
- PoE support
- AI features
- Easy scalability
- Remote management

Suitable for

- New installations
- Commercial projects
- Enterprise surveillance

Analog Cameras

Advantages

- Lower initial cost
- Reuse existing coaxial cable
- Simple installation

Suitable for

- Existing analog systems
- Budget upgrades

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 3: Choose Resolution

2MP

Suitable for

- Basic home monitoring
- Small shops
- Indoor surveillance

Provides Full HD image quality.

4MP

Suitable for

- Homes
- Offices
- Retail stores

Provides higher detail than 2MP.

5MP

Suitable for

- Entrances
- Cash counters
- Warehouses

Offers improved clarity for identification.

8MP (4K)

Suitable for

- Large commercial buildings
- Parking lots
- Industrial facilities

Recommended where detailed identification is required.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 4: Select Camera Style

Bullet Camera

Best for

- Outdoor walls
- Perimeter protection
- Parking areas

Advantages

- Visible deterrent
- Long viewing distance

--------------------------------------------------

Dome Camera

Best for

- Offices
- Indoor areas
- Reception
- Retail

Advantages

- Compact appearance
- Difficult to tamper with

--------------------------------------------------

Turret Camera

Best for

- Homes
- Offices
- Shops

Advantages

- Excellent night vision
- Minimal IR reflection

--------------------------------------------------

PTZ Camera

Best for

- Warehouses
- Stadiums
- Campuses
- Airports

Advantages

- Pan
- Tilt
- Optical Zoom
- Auto Tracking

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 5: Indoor or Outdoor

Indoor cameras generally do not require weatherproof housing.

Outdoor cameras should typically have weather-resistant enclosures suitable for rain, dust, and varying temperatures.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 6: Night Vision

Choose cameras with infrared or full-color night vision depending on lighting conditions and application requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 7: Audio Recording

Some cameras include

- Built-in microphone
- Audio input
- Two-way audio

Always comply with applicable privacy laws before recording audio.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 8: Storage Planning

Storage depends on

- Number of cameras
- Resolution
- Recording schedule
- Frame rate
- Compression
- Retention period

Higher resolution generally requires more storage capacity.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 9: Remote Viewing

Most modern surveillance systems support secure remote monitoring using manufacturer-supported mobile applications and desktop software.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 10: AI Features

Modern cameras may include

- Human Detection
- Vehicle Detection
- Line Crossing Detection
- Intrusion Detection
- Face Detection
- License Plate Recognition
- Smart Search

Feature availability depends on the camera model.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 11: Power Options

Available methods include

- PoE
- 12V DC
- 24V AC

PoE simplifies installation by carrying power and data over a single Ethernet cable.

--------------------------------------------------

## Step 12: Choosing the Right System

# Frequently Asked Questions

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is CCTV?

A: CCTV (Closed Circuit Television) is a video surveillance system used to monitor homes, offices, retail stores, warehouses, factories, educational institutions, hospitals, parking areas, and public spaces. Modern CCTV systems allow live viewing, recording, playback, remote monitoring, and intelligent video analytics.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is an IP camera?

A: An IP camera is a network-based surveillance camera that transmits digital video over an Ethernet or Wi-Fi network. IP cameras generally provide higher image quality, support PoE, enable remote management, and often include AI-powered detection features.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is an analog camera?

A: Analog cameras transmit video over coaxial cable to a Digital Video Recorder (DVR). They are commonly used for upgrading existing CCTV installations where coaxial cabling is already available.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which is better: IP camera or analog camera?

A: The choice depends on the project. IP cameras typically offer higher image quality, AI features, easier scalability, and network integration. Analog cameras are often suitable for budget-conscious projects or existing coaxial installations.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a DVR?

A: A DVR (Digital Video Recorder) records video from analog CCTV cameras. It stores recordings on surveillance hard drives and allows playback, remote viewing, and video backup.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is an NVR?

A: An NVR (Network Video Recorder) records video from IP cameras over a network. Many NVRs support advanced features such as AI search, remote management, PoE, and higher recording resolutions.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is PoE?

A: PoE (Power over Ethernet) allows both electrical power and network data to be transmitted through a single Ethernet cable, simplifying installation and reducing cable requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is ONVIF?

A: ONVIF is an industry standard that helps products from different manufacturers communicate with each other. Compatibility may vary depending on supported ONVIF profiles and device capabilities.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What does H.265 mean?

A: H.265 is a video compression standard that generally provides better compression efficiency than H.264, allowing longer recording times while maintaining similar image quality.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What resolution should I choose?

A: The ideal resolution depends on the application. 2MP is suitable for basic surveillance, 4MP offers improved detail, 5MP provides better identification, and 8MP (4K) is commonly used where maximum image clarity is required.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which camera is best for home security?

A: The best choice depends on the property layout, lighting conditions, budget, desired image quality, storage requirements, and whether features such as AI detection, remote viewing, or audio recording are needed.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which camera is best for an office?

A: Offices commonly use IP dome cameras for indoor areas, bullet cameras for outdoor coverage, and access control systems for secure entry management.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which camera is best for a warehouse?

A: Warehouses often require bullet cameras for perimeter monitoring, dome cameras for indoor aisles, and PTZ cameras for monitoring large open spaces.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: How many cameras do I need?

A: The number depends on the size of the property, the number of entrances, parking areas, hallways, storage locations, and security objectives. A site survey helps determine appropriate coverage.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: How long will CCTV footage be stored?

A: Recording duration depends on factors including the number of cameras, recording resolution, frame rate, compression, recording schedule, and hard drive capacity.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV work without the internet?

A: Yes. Local recording generally continues without an internet connection. Internet access is typically required only for remote viewing, cloud services, and certain online features.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can I view my CCTV cameras on my phone?

A: Most modern surveillance systems support remote viewing through manufacturer-provided mobile applications, provided the system is correctly configured and connected to the internet.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV record at night?

A: Yes. Many cameras include infrared night vision or full-color low-light technologies designed for surveillance in low-light conditions.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a bullet camera?

A: A bullet camera is a cylindrical surveillance camera commonly used outdoors. Its visible design often acts as a deterrent and is well suited for monitoring long distances.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a dome camera?

A: A dome camera is a compact camera commonly installed on ceilings. It is frequently used indoors in offices, retail stores, hotels, schools, and hospitals.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a turret camera?

A: A turret camera combines the flexibility of a bullet camera with the compact design of a dome camera and is often chosen for its excellent night vision performance.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a PTZ camera?

A: PTZ stands for Pan-Tilt-Zoom. These cameras can rotate horizontally, tilt vertically, and zoom optically, making them suitable for monitoring large areas.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Do CCTV cameras record audio?

A: Some camera models include built-in microphones or support external microphones. Audio recording capabilities vary by product and should always be used in compliance with applicable laws and privacy requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras detect people?

A: Many modern AI-enabled cameras include human detection features that help reduce false alarms by distinguishing people from general motion.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras detect vehicles?

A: Many AI-enabled surveillance cameras support vehicle detection and can classify vehicles separately from people, depending on the model and configuration.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Is 2MP enough for home security?

A: A 2MP camera is suitable for many basic residential surveillance applications. However, if greater detail is required for identifying faces, vehicles, or distant objects, higher resolutions such as 4MP or 8MP may be more appropriate.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Is 4MP better than 2MP?

A: Yes. A 4MP camera generally captures more detail than a 2MP camera, making it easier to identify people, objects, and vehicles while allowing greater flexibility when digitally zooming into recorded footage.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Is 5MP better than 4MP?

A: A 5MP camera provides a higher pixel count than a 4MP camera. The practical difference depends on lens quality, image processing, lighting conditions, and the viewing distance.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Should I buy 4K CCTV cameras?

A: 4K (8MP) cameras are suitable where maximum image detail is required, such as warehouses, parking lots, industrial facilities, and large commercial properties. They generally require more storage and network bandwidth than lower-resolution cameras.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which camera is better for outdoor use?

A: Outdoor surveillance typically requires weather-resistant cameras with appropriate ingress protection, night vision capabilities, and a viewing angle suitable for the area being monitored.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Which camera is better for indoor use?

A: Dome and turret cameras are commonly used indoors because of their compact design and wide viewing angles.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is an IP66 rating?

A: IP66 indicates that a device is protected against dust ingress and powerful water jets. Always verify the manufacturer's specifications for the exact environmental rating of a product.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is an IP67 rating?

A: IP67 indicates protection against dust and temporary immersion in water under specified conditions as defined by the manufacturer.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: How much hard drive storage do I need?

A: Storage requirements depend on the number of cameras, recording resolution, compression standard, frame rate, recording schedule, and the desired retention period. Larger systems generally require higher-capacity surveillance hard drives.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can one hard drive support multiple cameras?

A: Yes. A single surveillance hard drive can store recordings from multiple cameras, provided the recorder supports the required capacity and recording workload.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can I add more cameras later?

A: Expansion depends on the available channels in the DVR or NVR, network capacity, power availability, and storage resources.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can IP and analog cameras be used together?

A: Some hybrid recorders support both IP and analog cameras. Compatibility depends on the recorder model and manufacturer specifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is a hybrid DVR?

A: A hybrid DVR supports combinations of analog and IP cameras, allowing gradual migration from older analog systems to network-based surveillance.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is remote viewing?

A: Remote viewing allows authorized users to monitor live video and recorded footage from smartphones, tablets, or computers through manufacturer-supported applications or software.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Does CCTV work during a power failure?

A: Cameras and recorders require electrical power. Backup solutions such as UPS systems or inverter systems can help maintain operation during power interruptions.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras record continuously?

A: Most systems support continuous recording, scheduled recording, motion-triggered recording, or combinations of these modes.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is motion detection?

A: Motion detection records or alerts when movement is detected within configured areas. AI-enabled systems may distinguish between humans, vehicles, and general motion.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is human detection?

A: Human detection uses artificial intelligence to identify people while reducing false alerts caused by animals, shadows, rain, or moving vegetation, depending on the product capabilities.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is vehicle detection?

A: Vehicle detection uses AI to recognize motor vehicles separately from other moving objects, enabling more accurate event notifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is line crossing detection?

A: Line crossing detection generates an event when a person or vehicle crosses a virtual line configured within the camera's field of view.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is intrusion detection?

A: Intrusion detection monitors predefined areas and can generate alerts when people or vehicles enter restricted zones.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is face detection?

A: Face detection identifies the presence of human faces within the camera image. Some advanced systems also support face recognition, depending on hardware and software capabilities.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What is license plate recognition?

A: License Plate Recognition (LPR/ANPR) uses specialized cameras and software to detect and read vehicle registration numbers under supported conditions.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Are CCTV cameras waterproof?

A: Many outdoor cameras are designed with weather-resistant housings. Always verify the IP rating and manufacturer specifications before outdoor installation.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras be installed on ceilings?

A: Yes. Dome and turret cameras are commonly ceiling-mounted, while bullet cameras may be mounted on walls, poles, or ceilings depending on the installation requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras be mounted on poles?

A: Yes. Pole-mounted installations typically use manufacturer-approved mounting brackets designed for the camera model and pole diameter.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras monitor parking areas?

A: Yes. Parking surveillance commonly uses bullet cameras, panoramic cameras, or PTZ cameras depending on the size and layout of the area.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: Can CCTV cameras monitor warehouses?

A: Yes. Warehouses often use a combination of fixed cameras and PTZ cameras to cover entrances, loading bays, storage racks, and open spaces.

--------------------------------------------------

Q: What frame rate should I choose?

A: The appropriate frame rate depends on the application. Higher frame rates provide smoother video but require more storage and network bandwidth.

# DVR vs NVR Guide

Digital Video Recorders (DVR) and Network Video Recorders (NVR) are the two most common methods of recording surveillance footage.

Understanding their differences helps customers choose the appropriate system for their project.

--------------------------------------------------

## What is a DVR?

A DVR records video from analog CCTV cameras.

The cameras send video through coaxial cable to the recorder.

The DVR processes, compresses and stores the footage.

Typical Applications

- Existing analog installations
- Budget-friendly projects
- Small residential installations
- Shops
- Small offices

--------------------------------------------------

## What is an NVR?

An NVR records video from IP cameras connected through a network.

Video is transmitted digitally over Ethernet instead of coaxial cable.

Many NVR systems support advanced AI features depending on the camera and recorder.

Typical Applications

- New installations
- Offices
- Apartments
- Warehouses
- Factories
- Educational institutions
- Enterprise surveillance

--------------------------------------------------

## Cabling

DVR

Uses coaxial cable for video transmission.

Power is generally supplied separately.

Common cables

- RG59
- RG6

--------------------------------------------------

NVR

Uses Ethernet cable.

Many installations use PoE where both power and data travel through a single cable.

Common cables

- Cat5e
- Cat6
- Cat6A

--------------------------------------------------

## Image Quality

Both DVR and NVR systems can support high-resolution cameras.

Actual image quality depends on

- Camera resolution
- Sensor quality
- Lens quality
- Lighting
- Compression
- Installation

--------------------------------------------------

## Installation

DVR

Usually easier when upgrading older analog systems.

NVR

Often preferred for new installations due to simplified Ethernet wiring and network scalability.

--------------------------------------------------

## Expansion

DVR

Expansion is generally limited by available recorder channels.

NVR

Network-based systems are often easier to expand depending on recorder capacity and network design.

--------------------------------------------------

## Remote Viewing

Both DVR and NVR systems commonly support

- Mobile applications
- Web access
- Desktop software

Availability depends on manufacturer support.

--------------------------------------------------

## AI Features

Modern NVR systems often support

- Human Detection
- Vehicle Detection
- Face Detection
- Smart Search
- Intrusion Detection
- Line Crossing
- License Plate Recognition

Some DVR systems also support AI depending on the recorder and camera models.

--------------------------------------------------

## Storage

Both systems generally record onto surveillance hard drives.

Recording duration depends on

- Resolution
- Number of cameras
- Frame rate
- Compression
- Recording schedule

--------------------------------------------------

## Which should I choose?

Choose DVR if

- Existing coaxial wiring is available
- Replacing an older DVR
- Budget is a primary consideration

Choose NVR if

- Building a new surveillance system
- Higher flexibility is required
- IP cameras are preferred
- Future expansion is expected
- Advanced AI features are important

--------------------------------------------------

## Advantages of DVR

- Compatible with analog cameras
- Suitable for existing coaxial installations
- Lower upgrade cost in many retrofit projects

--------------------------------------------------

## Advantages of NVR

- Network-based architecture
- Simplified PoE installation
- Easier scalability
- Better integration with enterprise networks
- Supports many modern AI capabilities

--------------------------------------------------

## Frequently Asked Questions

Can DVR support IP cameras?

Some hybrid DVR models support both analog and IP cameras. Compatibility depends on the specific recorder.

Can I replace a DVR with an NVR?

Yes, although IP cameras and Ethernet cabling may also be required unless hybrid solutions are used.

Which is better for home security?

Both can provide effective surveillance. The appropriate choice depends on budget, existing wiring, desired features, and future expansion requirements.

Which is better for business?

Many new commercial installations prefer IP camera systems with NVRs because of scalability, image quality, and advanced analytics.

# PoE vs Non-PoE CCTV Cameras

Power over Ethernet (PoE) is one of the most common technologies used in modern IP surveillance systems.

Understanding the differences between PoE and non-PoE cameras helps customers select the most suitable solution for their installation.

--------------------------------------------------

## What is PoE?

PoE (Power over Ethernet) allows both electrical power and network data to be transmitted through a single Ethernet cable.

Instead of using separate power adapters for each camera, a PoE switch or PoE-enabled NVR supplies power through the network cable.

--------------------------------------------------

## How PoE Works

A PoE switch or PoE injector sends power and network connectivity through a standard Ethernet cable.

The IP camera receives both power and data using one cable.

This simplifies installation while reducing cable clutter.

--------------------------------------------------

## What is a Non-PoE Camera?

A non-PoE IP camera still transmits video over a network cable but requires a separate power source.

Power may be supplied using

- DC Adapter
- Centralized Power Supply
- Power Distribution Box

--------------------------------------------------

## Cabling Comparison

PoE Camera

One Ethernet cable

Carries

- Power
- Network Data

--------------------------------------------------

Non-PoE Camera

Ethernet cable

plus

Power cable

--------------------------------------------------

## Installation

PoE

Advantages

- Fewer cables
- Faster installation
- Cleaner wiring
- Easier maintenance

--------------------------------------------------

Non-PoE

Advantages

- Existing power infrastructure can be reused
- Suitable where PoE equipment is unavailable

--------------------------------------------------

## Reliability

Both systems can provide reliable surveillance when designed and installed correctly.

System reliability depends on

- Cable quality
- Power quality
- Network design
- Environmental conditions
- Equipment compatibility

--------------------------------------------------

## Maintenance

PoE installations generally simplify troubleshooting because both power and data originate from centralized equipment.

Non-PoE installations may require checking both network connectivity and local power supplies.

--------------------------------------------------

## Maximum Cable Length

Standard Ethernet installations typically support cable lengths up to approximately 100 meters between network devices.

Longer distances generally require additional networking equipment or fiber optic infrastructure.

--------------------------------------------------

## Power Consumption

Different cameras require different power levels.

Examples include

- Fixed cameras
- PTZ cameras
- Thermal cameras
- Multi-sensor cameras

Always verify the manufacturer's power requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## PoE Standards

Common IEEE standards include

802.3af

Typically supports lower-power devices.

--------------------------------------------------

802.3at (PoE+)

Supports devices requiring higher power.

--------------------------------------------------

802.3bt

Designed for higher-power equipment such as

- PTZ cameras
- Multi-sensor cameras
- Specialized surveillance devices

--------------------------------------------------

## PoE Switches

PoE switches are available in various port configurations.

Common sizes include

- 4 Port
- 8 Port
- 16 Port
- 24 Port
- 48 Port

Features may include

- Gigabit Ethernet
- Managed Switching
- VLAN
- QoS
- Long Range PoE
- Cloud Management

--------------------------------------------------

## PoE Injectors

PoE injectors add power to a single Ethernet connection.

They are commonly used when replacing a single camera without changing the existing switch.

--------------------------------------------------

## PoE Splitters

PoE splitters separate power and data for devices that do not natively support PoE.

--------------------------------------------------

## Advantages of PoE

- Single cable installation
- Reduced wiring complexity
- Centralized power management
- Simplified maintenance
- Easier future expansion
- Cleaner equipment rooms

--------------------------------------------------

## Advantages of Non-PoE

- Can reuse existing power wiring
- Suitable for certain legacy installations
- Compatible with cameras that require dedicated power supplies

--------------------------------------------------

## Typical Applications

PoE

Commonly used for

- Offices
- Apartments
- Educational Institutions
- Warehouses
- Commercial Buildings
- Hotels
- Hospitals

--------------------------------------------------

Non-PoE

Commonly used for

- Existing installations
- Retrofit projects
- Locations with available local power

--------------------------------------------------

## Frequently Asked Questions

Do all IP cameras support PoE?

No.

Support depends on the individual camera model and manufacturer specifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Can PoE damage a camera?

Standards-compliant PoE equipment is designed to negotiate power safely with compatible devices.

Always use equipment that follows recognized standards and manufacturer recommendations.

--------------------------------------------------

Do I need a PoE switch?

Only if the camera requires PoE and power is being supplied over the Ethernet cable.

Some installations instead use PoE injectors or PoE-enabled NVRs.

--------------------------------------------------

Can one PoE switch power many cameras?

Yes.

The number of supported cameras depends on

- Available ports
- Total PoE power budget
- Power consumption of each connected device

--------------------------------------------------

Should I choose PoE for a new installation?

PoE is commonly selected for new IP surveillance installations because it simplifies cabling, centralizes power management, and supports easier expansion.

The final choice should consider project requirements, infrastructure, and budget.

--------------------------------------------------

Summary

PoE systems reduce installation complexity by combining power and data over one cable.

Non-PoE systems remain suitable for many retrofit or specialized installations.

The most appropriate solution depends on existing infrastructure, equipment compatibility, installation environment, and long-term expansion plans.

# Home CCTV Planning Guide

This guide provides general recommendations for planning CCTV surveillance in residential properties.

Every property is different. Camera placement, equipment selection, storage requirements, and recording settings should be based on the actual site layout and security objectives.

--------------------------------------------------

## Security Objectives

Before selecting equipment, identify what you want to monitor.

Common objectives include

- Main entrance
- Front gate
- Driveway
- Parking area
- Living room
- Backyard
- Terrace
- Side passage
- Balcony
- Staircase
- Garden

--------------------------------------------------

## Apartment Surveillance

Apartments generally require fewer cameras than independent houses.

Typical monitoring areas include

- Main entrance
- Doorway
- Living room
- Balcony

Depending on apartment regulations, cameras covering common areas should comply with applicable housing society rules and local privacy requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Independent House

Typical monitoring areas

- Front gate
- Main entrance
- Parking
- Side passage
- Backyard
- Terrace access

Outdoor cameras should be selected according to the environmental conditions and desired coverage.

--------------------------------------------------

## Villa Surveillance

Larger villas may require surveillance for

- Compound wall
- Gate
- Garden
- Swimming pool
- Parking
- Main entrance
- Rear entrance
- Terrace
- Service entrance

Coverage planning should minimize blind spots while respecting privacy.

--------------------------------------------------

## Indoor Cameras

Indoor cameras are commonly installed in

- Living room
- Entrance lobby
- Hallway
- Home office
- Store room

Bedrooms and bathrooms generally require additional consideration due to privacy expectations and applicable laws.

--------------------------------------------------

## Outdoor Cameras

Outdoor cameras commonly monitor

- Gate
- Parking
- Compound
- Backyard
- Terrace
- Garden

Outdoor installations should use products suitable for the expected environmental conditions.

--------------------------------------------------

## Camera Placement Principles

General recommendations include

- Install cameras at an appropriate height.
- Avoid direct sunlight into the lens where possible.
- Minimize backlighting.
- Reduce blind spots.
- Ensure stable mounting.
- Keep lenses clean.
- Avoid unnecessary obstructions.

--------------------------------------------------

## Entry Points

Entrances are typically considered the highest priority surveillance locations.

These include

- Main door
- Rear door
- Side entrance
- Gate
- Garage entrance

--------------------------------------------------

## Parking Areas

Parking surveillance may benefit from

- Wide-angle coverage
- Adequate night visibility
- Appropriate camera height
- Sufficient lighting where practical

--------------------------------------------------

## Night Surveillance

Low-light monitoring depends on

- Ambient lighting
- Camera capabilities
- Lens characteristics
- Scene conditions

Infrared or low-light imaging technologies may be appropriate depending on the application.

--------------------------------------------------

## Remote Monitoring

Many modern surveillance systems support

- Smartphone viewing
- Tablet viewing
- Desktop software
- Event notifications

Availability depends on the selected equipment and configuration.

--------------------------------------------------

## Internet Connection

Internet connectivity is generally required for remote viewing and cloud-based features.

Local recording can typically continue without internet access if power remains available.

--------------------------------------------------

## Power Backup

Where uninterrupted recording is important, backup power solutions may be considered for

- Cameras
- Recorders
- Network equipment
- Internet equipment

System design depends on the required backup duration.

--------------------------------------------------

## Storage Planning

Storage requirements depend on

- Number of cameras
- Resolution
- Recording mode
- Frame rate
- Compression
- Retention period

Longer retention periods generally require greater storage capacity.

--------------------------------------------------

## Motion Recording

Motion-triggered recording may reduce storage usage by recording events instead of continuous video.

Performance depends on scene activity and detection settings.

--------------------------------------------------

## Continuous Recording

Continuous recording provides uninterrupted footage but requires additional storage.

--------------------------------------------------

## Privacy Considerations

Camera placement should respect the privacy of occupants, neighbors, and visitors.

Users should comply with applicable local laws and regulations regarding surveillance and audio recording.

--------------------------------------------------

## Common Mistakes

Avoid

- Installing cameras too high
- Pointing cameras directly at bright lights
- Ignoring night-time lighting
- Leaving blind spots
- Using insufficient storage
- Selecting inappropriate lens angles
- Poor cable management
- Skipping routine maintenance

--------------------------------------------------

## Recommended Planning Process

1. Identify important areas.
2. Determine indoor and outdoor coverage.
3. Estimate camera quantity.
4. Select suitable camera types.
5. Plan network and power infrastructure.
6. Estimate storage requirements.
7. Plan remote access if required.
8. Consider future expansion.
9. Review privacy considerations.
10. Perform periodic maintenance after installation.

--------------------------------------------------

Summary

An effective residential CCTV system should balance image quality, coverage, storage, reliability, maintenance, privacy, and future scalability according to the property's specific requirements.

# CCTV Storage Planning Guide

Selecting the correct storage capacity is an important part of surveillance system planning.

Insufficient storage may reduce recording retention, while excessive storage may increase project cost unnecessarily.

Actual storage requirements depend on several technical and operational factors.

--------------------------------------------------

## Factors Affecting Storage

Recording duration is influenced by

- Number of cameras
- Camera resolution
- Frame rate (FPS)
- Video compression
- Scene complexity
- Bitrate
- Recording schedule
- Motion activity
- Retention period

--------------------------------------------------

## Number of Cameras

Increasing the number of cameras generally increases storage requirements.

Example installations

- 2 Cameras
- 4 Cameras
- 8 Cameras
- 16 Cameras
- 32 Cameras
- 64 Cameras

Each additional camera contributes additional storage usage depending on its recording configuration.

--------------------------------------------------

## Camera Resolution

Higher resolutions typically require more storage.

Common resolutions include

- 2MP
- 4MP
- 5MP
- 6MP
- 8MP (4K)
- 12MP

The actual storage increase depends on bitrate, compression, scene complexity, and recording settings.

--------------------------------------------------

## Frame Rate

Higher frame rates produce smoother video but generally require more storage.

Typical frame rates

- 10 FPS
- 15 FPS
- 20 FPS
- 25 FPS
- 30 FPS

Many surveillance applications operate effectively at moderate frame rates depending on the security objective.

--------------------------------------------------

## Video Compression

Common compression standards include

- H.264
- H.265
- H.265+

More efficient compression generally reduces storage requirements while maintaining comparable image quality.

Actual performance depends on camera capabilities and recording settings.

--------------------------------------------------

## Continuous Recording

Continuous recording stores video throughout the day.

Advantages

- Complete recording history
- No missed events
- Suitable for high-security environments

Considerations

- Higher storage usage
- Greater hard drive capacity may be required

--------------------------------------------------

## Motion Recording

Motion-based recording stores footage only when activity is detected.

Advantages

- Reduced storage usage
- Longer retention periods
- Faster review of events

Effectiveness depends on motion detection settings and scene activity.

--------------------------------------------------

## Scheduled Recording

Recording schedules allow recording only during selected periods.

Typical examples include

- Business hours
- Night-time only
- Weekdays
- Weekends
- Holiday schedules

--------------------------------------------------

## Scene Complexity

Busy environments often generate larger video files.

Examples

Higher storage usage

- Busy roads
- Parking lots
- Shopping malls
- Factory floors

Lower storage usage

- Corridors
- Storage rooms
- Server rooms
- Restricted areas

--------------------------------------------------

## Retention Period

Organizations often define how long recordings should remain available.

Example retention targets

- 7 days
- 15 days
- 30 days
- 60 days
- 90 days

Requirements may vary depending on organizational policies or applicable regulations.

--------------------------------------------------

## Hard Drive Selection

Surveillance systems generally use hard drives designed for continuous recording workloads.

Typical capacities include

- 1 TB
- 2 TB
- 4 TB
- 6 TB
- 8 TB
- 10 TB
- 12 TB
- 16 TB
- 20 TB

Always verify recorder compatibility before selecting a drive.

--------------------------------------------------

## RAID Storage

Some enterprise recorders support RAID configurations.

Potential benefits include

- Increased reliability
- Improved fault tolerance
- Larger storage pools

RAID is not a substitute for backups.

--------------------------------------------------

## Network Attached Storage (NAS)

Some surveillance systems support recording to compatible NAS devices.

NAS may be suitable for

- Centralized storage
- Larger deployments
- Extended retention

Compatibility depends on the recorder and storage platform.

--------------------------------------------------

## Backup

Important recordings should be backed up when appropriate.

Common backup methods include

- USB Storage
- External Hard Drive
- Network Storage
- Cloud Storage (where supported)

--------------------------------------------------

## Storage Planning Workflow

General planning steps

1. Determine the number of cameras.
2. Select camera resolutions.
3. Choose recording mode.
4. Define frame rates.
5. Select compression settings.
6. Decide the required retention period.
7. Estimate storage requirements.
8. Verify recorder compatibility.
9. Consider future expansion.
10. Review backup requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Frequently Asked Questions

Can I add another hard drive later?

Expansion depends on the recorder model, available drive bays, supported capacities, and manufacturer specifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Will a larger hard drive improve video quality?

No.

Image quality depends primarily on camera resolution, sensor performance, lens quality, lighting, and recording configuration.

--------------------------------------------------

Does motion recording save storage?

Yes.

Motion-triggered recording generally reduces storage usage compared with continuous recording, although actual savings depend on scene activity.

--------------------------------------------------

Can I replace a hard drive with a larger one?

Many recorders support hard drive upgrades within their supported capacity limits.

Always verify compatibility before upgrading.

--------------------------------------------------

Summary

Effective storage planning balances image quality, retention period, storage capacity, recording method, and future expansion while considering the operational needs of the surveillance system.

# CCTV Camera Lens Selection Guide

Selecting the correct lens is just as important as choosing the camera resolution.

A higher resolution camera cannot compensate for an inappropriate field of view or incorrect camera placement.

Lens selection should be based on the monitoring objective, installation distance, and area that needs to be covered.

--------------------------------------------------

## What is a Camera Lens?

The camera lens determines

- Viewing angle
- Field of view
- Magnification
- Coverage area
- Object size within the image

Different lens focal lengths provide different perspectives.

--------------------------------------------------

## Common Fixed Lens Sizes

Common surveillance lens sizes include

- 2.1 mm
- 2.5 mm
- 2.8 mm
- 3.6 mm
- 4 mm
- 6 mm
- 8 mm
- 12 mm
- 16 mm

Some cameras also include motorized varifocal lenses.

--------------------------------------------------

## 2.8 mm Lens

Characteristics

- Wide viewing angle
- Covers a larger area
- Objects appear smaller
- Suitable for short viewing distances

Typical Applications

- Living rooms
- Shops
- Reception areas
- Office entrances
- Small parking areas

--------------------------------------------------

## 3.6 mm Lens

Characteristics

- Balanced field of view
- Slightly narrower than 2.8 mm
- Improved object size at moderate distances

Applications

- Homes
- Offices
- Corridors
- Retail stores

--------------------------------------------------

## 4 mm Lens

Characteristics

- Narrower viewing angle
- Better detail at longer distances
- Smaller coverage area

Applications

- Entrances
- Driveways
- Gates
- Building entrances

--------------------------------------------------

## 6 mm Lens

Characteristics

- Longer viewing distance
- Narrow field of view
- Improved subject detail

Applications

- Parking areas
- Warehouses
- Boundary walls
- Loading bays

--------------------------------------------------

## 8 mm Lens

Suitable For

- Long driveways
- Large compounds
- Industrial facilities
- Property boundaries

--------------------------------------------------

## 12 mm Lens

Common Applications

- Long corridors
- Perimeter security
- Gate monitoring
- Large campuses

--------------------------------------------------

## Varifocal Lens

A varifocal lens allows the installer to adjust the focal length during installation.

Advantages

- Flexible viewing angle
- Optimized field of view
- Better installation accuracy

Typical Applications

- Warehouses
- Factories
- Parking facilities
- Commercial buildings
- Large entrances

--------------------------------------------------

## Motorized Varifocal Lens

Motorized varifocal cameras allow zoom adjustment through software without manually adjusting the lens.

Typical Features

- Remote zoom
- Remote focus
- Easier maintenance
- Flexible deployment

--------------------------------------------------

## Wide Angle Lenses

Advantages

- Larger coverage area
- Fewer cameras may be required
- Suitable for open spaces

Considerations

Objects appear smaller as the field of view increases.

--------------------------------------------------

## Narrow Angle Lenses

Advantages

- Better subject detail
- Improved identification at longer distances

Considerations

A narrower field of view covers less area.

--------------------------------------------------

## Choosing a Lens

The appropriate lens depends on

- Monitoring objective
- Camera mounting location
- Viewing distance
- Lighting conditions
- Identification requirements
- Available installation positions

--------------------------------------------------

## Common Applications

Apartment Entrance

Wide-angle lens often provides good entrance coverage.

--------------------------------------------------

Retail Store

Wide-angle lenses are commonly used to monitor customer areas.

--------------------------------------------------

Warehouse

A combination of wide-angle and longer focal length cameras may be appropriate depending on aisle length and storage layout.

--------------------------------------------------

Parking Area

Lens selection depends on parking size, vehicle movement, and desired level of detail.

--------------------------------------------------

Gate Monitoring

Longer focal length lenses may provide improved detail for vehicles and visitors approaching an entrance.

--------------------------------------------------

## Common Mistakes

Avoid

- Choosing the widest lens without considering identification requirements.
- Using a narrow lens when broad coverage is required.
- Ignoring camera mounting height.
- Ignoring viewing distance.
- Assuming higher megapixels eliminate the need for proper lens selection.
- Placing important subjects near the edge of the image where distortion may be greater.

--------------------------------------------------

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does a wider lens mean better quality?

No.

Lens focal length determines the field of view, while image quality also depends on the sensor, resolution, lighting, and image processing.

--------------------------------------------------

Is a 2.8 mm lens always better?

No.

A 2.8 mm lens covers more area, but objects appear smaller than with longer focal lengths.

--------------------------------------------------

Can I change the lens later?

Some cameras have interchangeable lenses or varifocal lenses, while many fixed-lens cameras do not.

Always verify the manufacturer's specifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Should I choose a varifocal camera?

Varifocal cameras provide flexibility during installation and may be beneficial where the optimal field of view is not known in advance.

--------------------------------------------------

Summary

Effective lens selection balances coverage area, viewing distance, subject detail, and installation environment to meet the surveillance objectives of the site.

# Night Vision Technologies Guide

Night-time surveillance is an important consideration when selecting CCTV cameras.

Different night vision technologies are designed for different lighting conditions and monitoring objectives.

The effectiveness of any night vision system depends on factors such as ambient light, camera sensor performance, lens quality, installation height, weather conditions, and scene complexity.

--------------------------------------------------

## Common Night Vision Technologies

Modern surveillance cameras may include one or more of the following technologies

- Infrared (IR) Night Vision
- White Light Illumination
- Full Color Night Vision
- Low Light Imaging
- Smart Hybrid Lighting

Available technologies vary by manufacturer and product model.

--------------------------------------------------

## Infrared (IR) Night Vision

Infrared cameras use infrared LEDs to illuminate the scene in low-light environments.

Characteristics

- Operates in darkness
- Produces monochrome images during IR operation
- Suitable for indoor and outdoor installations
- Available across a wide range of surveillance products

Typical Applications

- Homes
- Warehouses
- Parking Areas
- Offices
- Factories
- Schools

--------------------------------------------------

## Full Color Night Vision

Some surveillance cameras use large image sensors, wide-aperture lenses, and supplemental lighting to capture color images in low-light environments.

Characteristics

- Color images under supported lighting conditions
- Improved visual context
- Useful for identifying clothing, vehicles, and objects

Performance depends on available light and camera capabilities.

--------------------------------------------------

## White Light Cameras

White light cameras include visible LED illumination.

Characteristics

- Illuminates the monitored area
- May discourage unauthorized activity
- Supports color video under supported conditions

Considerations

Visible lighting may not be suitable for every installation.

--------------------------------------------------

## Smart Hybrid Lighting

Some cameras automatically switch between infrared and white light depending on scene conditions or detected events.

Features depend on the manufacturer and camera model.

--------------------------------------------------

## Low Light Imaging

Modern image sensors may provide improved performance in low-light environments without relying entirely on infrared illumination.

Performance varies according to

- Sensor technology
- Lens design
- Image processing
- Available ambient light

--------------------------------------------------

## Ambient Lighting

Night vision performance is influenced by

- Street lighting
- Building lighting
- Vehicle headlights
- Moonlight
- Indoor lighting
- Reflected light

Even small amounts of ambient light can significantly improve image quality.

--------------------------------------------------

## Weather Conditions

Environmental conditions may affect night-time surveillance.

Examples include

- Rain
- Fog
- Dust
- Smoke
- Snow
- Insects near illumination sources

These conditions may reduce image clarity depending on the installation.

--------------------------------------------------

## Camera Placement

Night performance may improve when

- Cameras avoid direct headlights.
- Strong light sources are not aimed directly into the lens.
- Cameras are mounted securely.
- Important subjects remain within the intended viewing area.

--------------------------------------------------

## Lens Selection

Lens focal length influences

- Viewing angle
- Subject size
- Available light reaching the image sensor

Appropriate lens selection should match the surveillance objective.

--------------------------------------------------

## Infrared Range

Manufacturers often specify an approximate infrared illumination distance.

Actual performance depends on

- Scene reflectivity
- Environmental conditions
- Camera settings
- Installation height

The published IR distance should be treated as an estimate rather than a guaranteed identification distance.

--------------------------------------------------

## Choosing the Right Technology

Residential

Infrared or full-color cameras may both be appropriate depending on lighting conditions and monitoring objectives.

--------------------------------------------------

Retail

Color night imaging may provide additional visual context for entrances and customer areas.

--------------------------------------------------

Warehouse

Infrared cameras are commonly used for large indoor areas, while supplemental lighting may be considered where greater color detail is required.

--------------------------------------------------

Parking Areas

Camera selection depends on

- Lighting availability
- Vehicle movement
- Desired identification level
- Installation layout

--------------------------------------------------

Industrial Facilities

A combination of fixed cameras, PTZ cameras, and appropriate lighting may be used depending on operational requirements.

--------------------------------------------------

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does infrared record in color?

Infrared operation typically produces monochrome images.

Some cameras switch between color and infrared modes depending on available light and camera design.

--------------------------------------------------

Is color night vision always better?

Not necessarily.

The most suitable technology depends on the lighting conditions, monitoring objective, and installation environment.

--------------------------------------------------

Do all cameras include night vision?

No.

Night vision capabilities vary by camera model and manufacturer.

Always verify the published specifications.

--------------------------------------------------

Can external lighting improve image quality?

Yes.

Appropriate lighting may improve image quality for many surveillance systems.

Lighting design should consider security objectives, energy usage, neighboring properties, and applicable regulations.

--------------------------------------------------

Will rain reduce night vision quality?

Rain, fog, dust, insects, and other environmental factors can influence image quality under certain conditions.

Proper camera placement and regular maintenance can help reduce these effects.

--------------------------------------------------

Summary

Selecting a night vision technology involves balancing lighting conditions, installation environment, camera capabilities, privacy considerations, and the intended security objectives.

The best solution depends on the specific application rather than a single technology.
